learn.canDo: Explain hosts, clients and servers, and compute why a shared protocol turns M times N integrations into M plus N.
learn.why: MCP is how tools reach models. Knowing what it standardises, and what it costs in context, is a current interview topic.
learn.keyIdea: Write the integration once, use it everywhere.

learn.canDo: Choose between stdio and streamable HTTP, and add authentication to a remote server.
learn.why: Where a server runs decides who can reach it and what it costs. Remote servers without auth are a common mistake.
learn.keyIdea: Local is one process per user; remote is shared and must be authenticated.

learn.canDo: Decide whether a capability should be a tool, a resource or a prompt, and say who controls each.
learn.why: Mapping capabilities to the right primitive is the core design decision when writing a server.
learn.keyIdea: Tools act, resources inform, prompts guide.

learn.canDo: Design an MCP server whose tools are task-shaped, trimmed, well-described, scoped per user and protocol-clean.
learn.why: Most servers fail from too many tools and noisy output. Design for the model, not for the API.
learn.keyIdea: Design tools for the model that reads them.

chapter.story: The assistant needs to reach the company's systems without a custom connector for each one.
outcomes: Pick a transport and secure it
Map capabilities to tools, resources and prompts
Build a server a model can use well
chapter.why: A model is only as useful as what it can reach. A shared protocol makes that reach cheap to build, and context cost is the price.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can explain MCP and design a server. At work you will decide which servers to connect and which to write.
